summary.headline: Shree Cement Q4 FY26 domestic volume rose 11% YoY to 10.56 Mt; EBITDA/ton up to INR1,125 with utilisation at 66%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 domestic cement volume reached 10.56 million tons, up about 25% QoQ and 11% YoY, while total volume including clinker was 10.77 Mt. Realisation rose 1.6% QoQ to INR4,725/ton and operating EBITDA rose 34% QoQ to INR1,212 crore (INR1,125/ton). For FY26, volume grew 2.2% to 36.4 Mt, realisation rose 3.6% to INR4,732/ton, and EBITDA was INR4,222 crore excluding a one-time INR80 crore hit. Management signalled a shift from price-led to volume-led growth, while flagging fuel and packing cost inflation from the Middle East conflict for Q1 FY27.

financial_highlights.change: +23.2% QoQ from 9.84 Mt; +9.4% per management's figures

financial_highlights.metric: Full-year sales volume (incl. Shree Cement East)

financial_highlights.value: INR4,222 crore (excl. one-time INR80 crore impact)
financial_highlights.change: +11% from INR3,814 crore; EBITDA/ton INR1,161 vs INR1,071

financial_highlights.value: INR6,400 crore net cash; ~INR1,500 crore borrowings; gross ~INR7,900 crore

segments.name: India cement (standalone + Shree Cement East)
segments.commentary: Q4 capacity utilisation 66% (North 70%, East 60%, South 61%) vs 56% in Dec 2025. Installed capacity reached 69.3 Mt after Kodla (Karnataka) integrated project of 3.65 Mt clinker and 3.5 Mt cement commissioned in the quarter.

segments.name: Union Cement (UAE)
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 45.65 lakh tons (+18%) and revenue AED 870 million (+39%). Sales slowed over the last two months due to Middle East tension; management expects recovery once peace returns. A 2.5 Mt cement mill is scheduled for September 2026.

segments.name: RMC business
segments.commentary: 26 plants operational at end-FY26; 10 more inaugurated in March 2026 and under commissioning, taking the count to 36. Q4 RMC revenue INR90 crore on 1.99 lakh m3; FY26 revenue INR246 crore. Management says it is too early to report RMC separately.

guidance_outlook: FY27 cement volume guided at about 40 Mt (management clarified this includes at most 0.2-0.3 Mt of clinker), versus 36.4 Mt in FY26.
FY27 capex estimated at about INR1,500 crore, covering RMC plants (target 50-55), railway sidings and preliminary Meghalaya work; the 80 Mt by FY29 target is retained but described as dynamic.
Depreciation guidance of INR1,600-1,700 crore for FY27 reaffirmed.

Fuel cost per kcal (landed) at INR1.60 in Q4 expected to rise 10-12% in Q1 FY27 to INR1.76-1.80; packing cost up about INR20/ton in Q4 with a further ~INR80-100/ton expected; management guided total cost impact of INR150-200/ton for Q1 FY27 vs March 2026. Q2 not commented on.
Price hikes of about INR25/bag taken in the past month, which management says covers anticipated cost increases up to June.
Management will move to consolidated reporting from next quarter.
capex_capacity: Kodla, Karnataka integrated project (3.65 Mt clinker, 3.5 Mt cement) commissioned in Q4 FY26; India installed capacity now 69.3 Mt.
Union Cement UAE 2.5 Mt cement mill scheduled for commissioning by September 2026.

Meghalaya integrated plant: 0.95 Mt clinker and 0.99 Mt cement; first block holds ~600 Mt limestone; ultimate capacity 4-4.5 Mt; capex about INR1,800 crore due to front-ended infrastructure. Mines are allocated by the state, not auctioned; no incentives confirmed yet.
Green power capacity 666.5 MW; green electricity 61% of consumption in Q4 FY26 (59% in Q4 FY25). Clinker factor 64.8% in Q4 (63.9% in Dec 2025).
Mauritius wholly owned subsidiary incorporated for cement, blending, storage and packing facilities.
demand_pricing: Management says the company has moved to a more stable pricing platform, narrowing the gap with the top player by INR15-20/bag, and is now pursuing volume share.
Q4 fuel mix: pet coke 54%, coal 32%, alternative fuel 14%. Trade sales 64% and blended cement 62% of volume (as stated in call).
Lead distance rose by about 12 km QoQ to 457 km in Q4, driving freight cost up roughly INR80/ton YoY and QoQ; target is below 440 km.
Management expects industry demand at 7.1-7.2% growth on 6.5% GDP assumption, with the company growing 1% above industry average.
Demand was healthy until 15 April 2026; slowdown since then, linked to Middle East conflict and moderate monsoon forecast.
Premium products share rose to 22% from 15% (about 9% two years ago).

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan and cash deployment given cash surplus near INR9,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex about INR1,500 crore (RMC, railway sidings, Meghalaya). Net cash INR6,400 crore and gross borrowings ~INR1,500 crore. Company has not borrowed for capex in about 15 years; plans to continue funding from internal accruals and may front-end capex if conditions improve.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 volume run rate match Q4's 11% growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance is about 40 Mt for FY27, including at most 0.2-0.3 Mt clinker; company targets 1% above industry growth, which management expects at 7.1-7.2%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the cost inflation outlook and how much is passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost per kcal to rise 10-12% in Q1 (INR1.60 to ~INR1.76-1.80). Packing cost up ~INR20/ton in Q4 and ~INR80-100/ton more ahead. Total Q1 cost impact INR150-200/ton. Price hikes of ~INR25/bag taken; management says these cover costs up to June, with Q2 not commented on.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 80 Mt by FY29 target still valid given utilisation in the low 60s?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says 80 Mt by 2029 is still on record but capex has slowed and the situation is dynamic; too early to say if it will slip.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company protect EBITDA/ton while chasing volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says profitability is the prime focus and it will not enter a price war; it has never given EBITDA/ton or price guidance.

qa_highlights.question: How does the company plan to cut costs (WHRS, RE, clinker factor, railway)?
qa_highlights.answer: All kilns have or will have WHRS; RE target not given (to be shared next call); BESS being explored; railway doubling being pursued at three to four sites without numbers; clinker factor said to be among the best in the industry.

risks_watch: Fuel and packing cost inflation: fuel 10-12% higher in Q1 and packing costs rising (PVC granules); management gave no Q2 view and cost pass-through depends on demand.
Demand slowdown since mid-April 2026 linked to Middle East conflict, steel and labour cost pressure, and a moderate monsoon forecast.
Lead distance (457 km in Q4) and freight cost pressure; management targets below 440 km.
Competitive pressure risk in the North as capacity is added, as flagged by a peer's chairman; management did not rule out share loss.
Meghalaya incentives not yet confirmed by the state government; project capex of INR1,800 crore.
Union Cement (UAE) sales slowed over the last two months; recovery depends on Middle East ceasefire holding.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and on pricing discipline, but noticeably evasive on Q2 FY27 costs, EBITDA/ton and North market share. Management repeatedly declined to quantify forward cost impact or give specific targets, saying the situation is dynamic.
key_quotes: We have delivered on both these accounts, which explains our ethos of delivery and not proclamation.
We have never in our history given any guidance on EBITDA per ton.
Profitability is the prime focus. Price always the market gives. Volume is what we are capable to produce.
Maybe next quarter onwards, we will talk of consol only.
